cgu.maj: 13 October 2026 (provisional — before a lawyer signs off; awaiting a second legal reading)

paras: Awzid is an application for learning Arabic, memorising the Quran (hifẓ) and basic religious education, which accompanies the Awzid books. These terms govern its use. During the closed beta, they apply together with the "Beta terms" and, for invited testers, the "Terms for invited testers".

Parent account: reserved for an adult; it creates the profiles of their children (nickname, year of birth, level) and gives the required consents. A child never has an e-mail address or an account in their own name.
Adult account: for an adult learner. A minor cannot open an adult account alone.

Teacher account: opened by the school, protected by a second factor. The teacher only sees the pupils enrolled in their class by their parent (class code and consent) or entered by the school (paper class).
Everyone keeps their password secret and does not share their access; the parent code protects settings and purchases. The information given at sign-up must be accurate.

The age from which a person can consent alone depends on the country (and, in Canada, the province). European regulation lets each State set it between 13 and 16, with 16 as the default. In Awzid: 15 in France, 16 in Germany, 14 in Spain, 13 in the United Kingdom and the United States, 14 in Quebec; 16 for a country not listed. [Values to be confirmed by the lawyer.]
Senegal: as a precaution, Awzid asks for the consent of a parent or guardian for anyone under 18. [Age to be confirmed by the lawyer: we did not find a digital consent age in law no. 2008-12.]

Below the age of the country, only a parent can create a child's profile and give consent; Awzid makes reasonable efforts to check that it is an adult (parent account with a verified address, parent code, dated and kept consent).
United States: during the beta, Awzid is not open to children under 13 (neither through a parent nor through a school).

Using Awzid (Quran, hifẓ, Islamic sciences) may reveal religious beliefs: an explicit consent, separate from these terms, is requested at sign-up, for each child profile, and from older accounts on first use. It can be withdrawn at any time; the account or profile is then paused (see the privacy policy).

The e-mail address is verified by a single-use link. If you forget your password, a link valid for 30 minutes is sent to the account address; the application's answer is the same whether the address is known or not.
An address change only takes place after confirmation from the new address; the old address is informed.
The Quran text shown comes only from the Tanzil reference text; no program writes or edits it. Hadiths are only shown if they are marked "verified" in the books' register.

During the beta, religious content whose scholarly review is not finished carries the mention "scholarly review in progress". It is provided for learning and replaces neither a qualified teacher nor a fatwa: if in doubt, ask a scholar or your teacher.

Any error can be reported ("Report a problem" → "A religious point to check", or "Report an error" under a verse, hadith or rule). Each religious correction is dated and published, with its source, on the "Errata" page.

The tutor is a program: it says so, gives no religious opinion and forwards religious questions to the teacher. It is off by default for children and only turns on with the parent's consent; the parent can read everything it said.
Certificates and attestations issued by a school are neither an ijāza nor a state diploma.

The application is meant for personal, family or school use. It is forbidden to copy, bulk-extract or redistribute the content (books, lessons, audio, third-party data), to bypass technical protections, to share an access code or an account, to disrupt the service, or to use it to spread illegal or hateful content, or content that distorts the Quran.
Third-party content (Quran text, translations, recitations, fonts) stays subject to its licences: you may not change or resell it.
During the beta, the application is free: no payment is requested or recorded (see the "Beta terms").

After the beta, a free plan will let you try the first lessons. Paid plans, their prices and duration will be shown before purchase; only the adult will be able to buy (parent code). No card data goes through Awzid: payment is made with the chosen provider.
The subscription can be stopped at any time; rights remain until the end of the paid period. [Right of withdrawal, refunds: to be completed according to the country and the provider.]

The application is provided with care but without any guarantee of uninterrupted or error-free service; during the beta, errors are expected. An account may be suspended for use that breaches these terms or the law, after informing its holder except in an emergency.
The holder can delete their account at any time from "My account": access is cut at once and data is permanently erased within 30 days.
A subscription taken in the App Store or on Google Play is not stopped by deleting the account: it must be cancelled in the store. The application reminds you before deletion.
Any significant change is announced in the application; if it affects a consent, a new consent is requested before continuing (dated version of the texts).
[Applicable law and competent court: to be completed by the lawyer — France or Senegal depending on the client's country.]

paras: [Company name and postal address: to be completed by the client]. Contact for your personal data: [e-mail address to be created by the client]. We answer any request about your data within 30 days. Data protection officer: [to be appointed if needed].

For a school using the school space (paper class, results, certificates), the school is the controller of the data it enters; Awzid acts on its behalf (processor). [Processing contract to be prepared.]

This policy applies to the whole application, including during the closed beta. Awzid uses content from Quran Foundation, the organisation behind Quran.com and QuranReflect (online recitations, Muṣḥaf layout); this content contains no data about you, and no Quran.com account is used.
Beta waiting list (home page): e-mail address and the language of the page, kept with your agreement, only to manage the waiting list and send you an invitation; no newsletter, no advertising.
Account: e-mail address and password (protected, never readable) of the adult; country; language; time zone.
Child profile: nickname, year of birth (never the full date), level, avatar — no real name, no photo, no address.
Learning: exercise answers, progress, hifẓ, letter tracings, word cards, working days of teens and adults.

Voice recordings: they stay on the device and are erased after 7 days; a family may choose to send one to the class teacher (withdrawable consent, parent code for a child): encrypted, heard by the teacher alone, never used to train an artificial intelligence.
School space: first name and initial of paper-class pupils, assessment marks, recitations, homework; full name entered only when a certificate is issued.
Payment (after the beta): plan, status and reference at the provider; never a card number.

Account security: links sent by e-mail (verification, forgotten password, address change) — only a fingerprint of the link is kept, with its use and date; IP address and a fingerprint of the e-mail address for 24 hours to limit abusive attempts.

Reports and feedback: category, description written by you (500 characters at most), the page you were on (path only), application version, role and age band (child, teen, adult); a screen image only if you attach it, taken on your device, private areas and input fields hidden. A child only sends the category. No name and no e-mail address in the report.
Tracker-free usage: daily totals of spaces or features used, without page address, time or device identifier.
Beta waiting list: your consent (the box on the home page, confirmed by a link sent to your address), which you can withdraw at any time by writing to the contact address.

Providing the requested service (performance of the contract); specific consents collected separately, dated and withdrawable (consent): follow-up by a teacher, sending a recitation, voice analysis, tutor, hosting outside Senegal for Senegalese holders, reminders; security, abuse prevention, handling of reports and improving the service (legitimate interest); accounting obligations after the beta (legal obligation).
No advertising, no commercial profiling, no resale of data, no behavioural personalisation for children.

sections.titre: Data revealing a religious belief (GDPR, Article 9)
paras: Learning the Quran, hifẓ or Islamic sciences with Awzid may reveal a religious belief, a special category of data. It is processed on the basis of your explicit consent (Article 9, paragraph 2, point a, of the GDPR), collected separately from the terms of use, by a box that is not ticked in advance, dated, with the version of the text and the proof of the consent.

In Senegal, law no. 2008-12 lists religious opinions or activities among sensitive data (Article 4) and forbids processing them except in specific cases, including express written consent (Articles 40 and 41). Awzid collects this consent in writing in the application.

Minimisation: Awzid never asks for your religion; it keeps only what is used for learning (progress, answers), with no analysis of beliefs, no profile, and no transmission to third parties other than the processors listed below. For a child, the consent is given by the parent, profile by profile.
You can withdraw this consent at any time in "My account": the account (or the profile concerned) is paused; nothing is erased unless you ask for deletion, and you can export your data.

sections.titre: Voice and automatic analysis by artificial intelligence
paras: "Recite and check" (a beta feature, reserved for some testers) can compare your recitation with the Quran text, word by word, using a speech recognition model that runs on Awzid's servers: the voice is processed in memory and is never kept. It gives no mark and no tajwīd opinion. It requires a separate consent, never ticked in advance and withdrawable; for a child, the parent code; it is refused to a minor registered alone.

An artificial intelligence tutor (language help) is planned but switched off during the beta: no data is sent to an AI provider today. If it is switched on later, it will use Gemini (Google) through Vertex AI, with no name or address, with a nickname, and only with your consent; this policy will be updated before it is switched on.

GDPR (Article 8): where consent is the basis for processing, a child under the age set by their country cannot consent alone; the regulation sets 16 and lets States go down to 13. In Awzid, a child's account is always opened and managed by a parent, and we make reasonable efforts to check that the consent really comes from a parent.
Ages used: 15 in France, 16 in Germany, 14 in Spain, 13 in the United Kingdom and the United States, 14 in Quebec, 16 by default. [To be confirmed by the lawyer.]

Senegal: as a precaution, every minor (under 18) goes through a parent. Processing complies with law no. 2008-12 of 25 January 2008; [declaration to the Personal Data Protection Commission (CDP): to be made by the client before opening to Senegalese users].

United States (COPPA): during the beta, no child profile under 13 is created; verifiable parental consent will be set up before any opening. Canada: in Quebec, the consent of the holder of parental authority is requested under 14; elsewhere in Canada, under 13. United Kingdom: most protective settings by default (notifications off, no tracker, no advertising). [To be confirmed by the lawyer.]
For parents: you can see and erase everything about your child, from "My account" and "Profiles".

Host: Google Cloud Platform, Paris region (europe-west9) — [link to its privacy policy: to be added by the client]. E-mail sending service: [to be chosen by the client, preferably in the European Union]. Payment providers (Stripe, PayPal, mobile money aggregator), after the beta and only if you pay. Browser notification service (Google, Mozilla, Apple…), only if you turn notifications on: the content is encrypted and contains no name. AI provider (Google, Gemini through Vertex AI): planned, switched off during the beta. Data processing contracts are concluded with processors that require them; each must respect the Quran and Islamic content (no use that distorts them). [To be checked by the client.]

Quran Foundation (quran.foundation): if you choose an "online" reciter, your device loads the audio files directly from Quran Foundation's servers, which then see the device's IP address and the technical information of an ordinary web request — never your name, account or profile. You may choose not to use these reciters.

Data region: each account and each school carries a data region label ("EU" today). Transfers outside the Union (notification service, AI provider if switched on) rely on the safeguards provided by the GDPR (standard contractual clauses or an adequacy decision). [To be checked.] For a Senegalese holder, hosting in France only takes place with their explicit consent; Article 49 of law no. 2008-12 also provides for informing the CDP of any transfer to a third country [declaration to be made by the client].

Beta waiting list: 12 months at most after the request (automatic deletion); 7 days if the address is never confirmed; or earlier on written request to the contact address. [To be confirmed by the lawyer.]
Deleted account: permanent erasure within 30 days; encrypted backups: the last 14, i.e. 14 rolling days (so fully purged 14 days after erasure).
Sessions: 30 days after expiry. Attempt locks: 24 hours. Links sent by e-mail: 30 minutes (forgotten password) or 24 hours (verification, address change), single use; erased with the account.
Tutor log: 12 months at most. Tutor questions and alerts: 12 months after handling, 24 months at most. Security audit log: 12 months.

Voice recordings: 7 days on the device; recitation sent to the teacher: erased after the period set by the class (14 days by default, 30 at most), or as soon as the family deletes it. AI voice analysis: no retention.
"Report a problem" reports: screen image erased after 90 days; a settled report erased after 12 months. Feedback: 12 months. Usage totals: daily aggregates, no person.
Proof of consent: account duration then 5 years (limitation period) [to be confirmed by the lawyer]. School ↔ family messages: 12 months after the end of the school year.

School certificate register: number, displayed name, level, date and mention kept long-term (proof of a diploma); the pupil's other data follow the periods above and the full document is reduced 30 days after the pupil leaves. [To be confirmed by the lawyer.]

Access, rectification, erasure, portability (full export in one file from "My account"), objection, restriction, withdrawal of a consent at any time, and, in Senegal, the rights of information, access, objection, rectification and deletion provided by Articles 58 to 69 of law no. 2008-12. To exercise them: "My account", or the contact address above; reply within 30 days.

Complaint: to the data protection authority of your country (CNIL in France, CDP in Senegal, the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada and the Commission d'accès à l'information in Quebec, ICO in the United Kingdom…).

Encrypted connection, protected passwords (argon2id), second factor for teachers and administration, separated database accounts, encryption of voices and messages, encrypted backups whose key is kept off the server, log of sensitive actions, keys and secrets limited to each service and renewed regularly [schedule: to be confirmed by the client].

In case of a data breach likely to harm your rights, Awzid notifies the competent protection authority as soon as possible, if feasible within 72 hours (GDPR, Article 33), and informs you directly if the risk is high. Every breach is recorded, and any security incident is handled within 24 hours (analysis and containment).
Any significant change is announced in the application (banner or e-mail) with the new update date; if it affects a consent, a new consent is requested.

cookies.maj: 13 October 2026 (provisional — before a lawyer signs off; awaiting a second legal reading)

paras: A single cookie: "awform_session", which keeps you signed in (strictly necessary, removed on sign-out or expiry).

On-device storage: local database "awform" and the application cache (downloaded lessons, answers waiting to be sent, 7-day voice recordings); browser local storage for your settings (light or dark mode, reader size and style, colour-coded tajwid, chosen riwāya, session in progress, copy of the feature switches, today's usage counter). All of this lets the application work offline and remember your choices; none of it is sent to another company.

No third-party cookie, no advertising tracker, no audience measurement by another company, no social network button, no font or resource loaded from another site. Only exception: if you choose an "online" reciter, the audio files come from Quran Foundation's servers (see the privacy policy).

sections.titre: Why there is no consent banner
paras: Cookies and storage strictly necessary for the service you request are exempt from consent (Article 82 of the French Data Protection Act; CNIL guidelines). Since nothing else is used, the application shows no banner. If a non-essential tracker were ever added, a banner (refusing as easy as accepting) would be mandatory before anything is placed. [To be confirmed by the lawyer.]
You can erase everything at any time from your browser settings (site data). You will be signed out and downloaded lessons will have to be downloaded again.

Verification and reset links carry their code in the part of the address that is never sent to the server (after "#"); the page removes it from the address bar as soon as it opens. No cookie is added.

paras: These terms are for people invited to test Awzid during the closed beta (family, pupils and teachers of the pilot school, reviewers, friends of the project). They add to the terms of use, the beta terms and the privacy policy.
The invitation (a code or a link) is personal: do not pass it on, do not publish it. Awzid may deactivate it at any time, and you may give it up at any time.
An invited adult creates their own account. For a child, the invited parent creates the profile and gives the consents; no child signs up alone.

Use the application normally, in good faith, and report what is wrong (bug, content to correct, religious point to check) with "Report a problem". Do not write a name, address or phone number in a report.

Do not copy, bulk-capture or share the content (books, lessons, audio, Quran, translations) beyond personal or family use. Do not try to bypass security or reach other people's data; if you find a flaw, tell us instead of using it.
Keep features still being tried confidential: they may change or disappear before public opening.

Protect your data as described in the privacy policy, charge you nothing, send you no advertising, read every report, publish religious corrections in "Errata", and warn you before the end of the beta.
Your reports and feedback may be used to improve the application; Awzid gains no right over your personal data, which remains yours.

Awzid may suspend access for use that breaches these terms, after informing you except in an emergency. You can leave the beta at any time by deleting your account from "My account" (erasure within 30 days).

The beta is provided as is, with no guarantee of availability or absence of errors; do not rely on it as your only learning tool. [Limitation of liability, applicable law: to be completed by the lawyer.]

The closed beta is a first version of Awzid, entrusted to a small number of invited people (family, pilot school, reviewers) before public opening. It is free, with no commitment, and your data can be erased at any time.
Awzid teaches Arabic, the Quran (Ḥafṣ reading, hifẓ, tajwid) and the basics of Islamic sciences (Mālikī school), for children, teenagers and adults, with or without a school.

The whole journey: creating an account, a child profile with the parent's consent, following the level's lessons, revising, memorising (hifẓ), reading and listening to the Quran, using the application offline.
How clear the screens are for children and families, reading on a phone, speed on a slow connection, and the accuracy of the religious content.
Features being tried (reserved for some testers): "I speak" and "Recite and check". Your comments on them are especially useful.
Some religious content is still under scholarly review and is marked as such; corrections are published on the "Errata" page.
Languages other than French are in preparation (interface translations to be reviewed); the legal texts are provisional.
The artificial intelligence tutor is off; payment is disabled; sending e-mails (verification, forgotten password) depends on the beta configuration.
Errors, slowness or awkward screens are possible. Test data may be reset at the end of the beta, with notice.

Help page → "Report a problem": choose a category (something does not work, content to correct, a religious point to check, other) and describe it in a few words, without name or address. The page you are on and the application version are attached automatically; a screen image is possible if you choose it. A child only chooses the category.
For an error in a verse, a hadith or a rule, use "Report an error" under the text: it is examined by the religious referent, and the correction is published in "Errata" with its source.
A question? See Help (frequent questions) or write to [beta contact address: to be created by the client].

items.q: Does my child need an e-mail address?
items.r: No. You create a parent account, then a profile for each child (nickname, year of birth, level). The child has no e-mail and no password to remember.

items.q: Where do I start?
items.r: Open "Today": the daily session suggests hifẓ, the current lesson and a few words to review, with the planned duration.

items.q: Does the application replace the books?
items.r: No, it accompanies them: same lessons, same corrected exercises, same hifẓ notebooks. The QR code of each lesson opens the matching page.

items.q: What is the beta and what should I do?
items.r: It is a trial version, free and by invitation. Use the application normally and report what is wrong (Help → "Report a problem"). See the page "The Awzid beta".

items.q: I forgot my password. What can I do?
items.r: On the sign-in screen, choose "Forgotten password": a link valid for 30 minutes is sent to the account's e-mail address (check your junk mail). The link works only once. If nothing arrives, ask for a new one or write to [contact address: to be created by the client].

items.q: I did not receive the verification e-mail.
items.r: Look in your junk mail, then ask for a link again from the screen that offered it. Also check that the address is spelled correctly in "My account".

items.q: How do I change my e-mail address?
items.r: In "My account": the change only takes place after confirmation from the new address, and the old address is informed.

items.q: How do we export or delete our data?
items.r: In "My account": full export in one file, account deletion (access cut at once, permanent erasure within 30 days). A subscription taken in the App Store or on Google Play must be stopped in the store.

items.q: How do I update the application?
items.r: When a new version is ready, a "New version available" banner appears: tap "Update". It never appears during a lesson or while listening. If you do not see it, close and reopen the application.

items.q: Can we work in airplane mode?
items.r: Yes. Download a level from "Downloads"; answers are sent on their own when the network returns, without losing anything or counting twice.

items.q: Does the application use a lot of data?
items.r: A whole level weighs less than 150 KB; "data saver" mode limits downloads even more. "Online" reciters are not downloaded and use more data.

items.q: The application is unavailable, what should I do?
items.r: A "service temporarily unavailable" page is shown during maintenance; lessons already downloaded remain usable offline. If the problem lasts, report it as soon as the network is back.

items.q: From what age can my child have their own account?
items.r: Never alone: a child's account is always created and managed by a parent. A teenager can open their own account from the age set by their country (15 in France); in Senegal, as a precaution, a parent's consent is requested up to 18.

items.q: Why do you ask for a "religious belief" consent?
items.r: Learning the Quran may reveal a religious belief, a particularly protected kind of data. We therefore ask for your explicit consent, separate from the terms. You can withdraw it in "My account": the account (or profile) is paused, nothing is erased without your request.

items.q: Can a child talk to the artificial intelligence or send messages?
items.r: The AI tutor is off during the beta. A child does not write free text in reports (they choose a category). School ↔ family messages are addressed to the family.

items.q: My child is in the United States. Can they sign up?
items.r: Not during the beta if they are under 13: opening to American children awaits verifiable parental consent.

items.q: Where does the Quran text come from?
items.r: From the Tanzil reference text (riwāya Ḥafṣ ʿan ʿĀṣim), compared sign by sign at each import; no program writes it.

items.q: What does "scholarly review in progress" mean?
items.r: The content is provided for learning but has not yet been reviewed by the scholars planned. For a question of practice, ask your teacher or a scholar. Corrections are published in "Errata".

items.q: I found an error in a religious text (verse, hadith, rule). How do I report it?
items.r: Under the text, tap "Report an error", or go to Help → "Report an error in a religious text". Say in one sentence what seems wrong (no name). The referent examines every report; if confirmed, the content is corrected (or hidden meanwhile) and the correction appears dated and sourced in "Errata".

items.q: Where can I see the corrections already made?
items.r: On the public "Errata" page: each religious correction is dated there, with its reference and edition. It is accessible without an account.

items.q: Who validates a recitation?
items.r: The teacher, with the notebooks' marking scale (mark out of 20). At home, the parent can listen with their parent code. The "Recite and check" feature (beta) never marks and never judges tajwid: only the teacher judges.

items.q: How do I enrol my child in their teacher's class?
items.r: The teacher gives you a class code; in "Profiles", you enter it for your child and give your consent. You can withdraw it at any time.

items.q: Is a certificate an ijāza?
items.r: No. Level certificates and recitation attestations record a course followed or a recitation validated in class; they are neither an ijāza nor a state diploma.

faq.titre: Reporting a problem and contacting us

items.q: How do I report a bug or a confusing screen?
items.r: Help → "Report a problem": category, a few words, and if you wish a screen image (taken on your device, private areas hidden). The page and the version are attached automatically. You must be signed in and online.

items.q: How do I contact you with a question or a request about my data?
items.r: Write to [contact address: to be created by the client]. We answer within 30 days. To export or erase your data, you can do it yourself in "My account".
